what_happened: The job "Baseline the checks before the producer; mark failures pre-existing" (20261018-070117-qmxv) ended failed. The producer stage hit its fixed 1800-second deadline before it finished, so the job stopped with no result. The event lists no unmet acceptance criteria, blocker or major findings, or failed checks. Nothing was delivered. The work is a code change to the job pipeline: it adds a baseline run of the repo checks before the producer starts and labels failures that were already there.
cause: The producer runs as one stage with a fixed wall-clock deadline that is not tied to the size of the job. Nothing estimates the work against the deadline, splits it into smaller pieces, saves partial progress, shows progress, or stops early with a partial result. A pipeline change that touches several stages (running checks, storing a baseline, comparing it, marking failures) is not split before it runs, so the overrun is found only after the full 1800 seconds are spent and all work is lost. This is a second code job in a row to fail this way. The registry class says "small, well-bounded", but the cause is wider: the deadline is not scaled to the job and there is no checkpoint or resume.
prevention: Make the producer stage resumable and size-aware. (1) Before the producer runs, a planning step must split any job with more than one separable deliverable into sub-jobs, each of which fits one deadline. (2) The producer must commit partial work to the job branch at checkpoints, and emit progress signals. (3) On deadline, the stage must record a timeout state with the partial diff and let a retry continue from it, not fail the whole job with nothing. This would have prevented both this job and the earlier add-roles job.
proposed_request: Make the producer stage survive its time deadline. Outcome: when a producer run reaches its deadline, the work done so far is kept (committed to the job branch or saved as a partial diff), the job is marked as timed out rather than failed, and a retry continues from the saved work instead of starting over. Also, before a producer runs, a job whose reading lists more than one separable deliverable is split into smaller jobs, each sized to finish within one deadline. Acceptance: a test with a producer forced to exceed a short deadline shows the partial work is preserved and a retry resumes from it; a test with a multi-deliverable reading shows it is split into several jobs. After this lands, re-submit "Baseline the checks before the producer; mark failures pre-existing" as separate jobs: first run the repo checks before the producer and record the result as a baseline; then mark a failing check as pre-existing when it also failed in the baseline.
